name: Kadane's Algorithm (Maximum Subarray)
description: Find the maximum (or minimum) sum contiguous subarray in O(n) by tracking a running sum that resets whenever continuing it would hurt more than starting fresh, rather than checking every possible subarray.
signal_phrases: best time to buy and sell stock
core_technique: Track `current_sum` (best sum of a subarray ending exactly at the current index) and `max_sum` (best seen anywhere so far). At each element, decide whether to extend the current subarray (current_sum + element) or start a new one at this element (just element) - whichever is larger. Update max_sum with current_sum after each step.
common_pitfalls: Initializing max_sum to 0 instead of negative infinity (or the first element) - this silently gives a wrong answer when all elements are negative, since the correct answer should be the least-negative single element, not 0; for the product variant, forgetting that a negative number flips max and min - you must track BOTH running max and running min product, since a very negative min times a new negative number can become the new max; resetting current_sum to 0 instead of comparing 'extend vs restart' properly.

example_problems.title: Maximum Subarray
example_problems.why_it_fits: The textbook Kadane's problem - at each index, decide whether extending the running subarray or starting fresh here gives a better sum.

example_problems.title: Maximum Product Subarray
example_problems.why_it_fits: Same running idea, but because a negative times a negative can become the largest product, you must track both a running max AND running min product at each step, swapping them when the current element is negative.

example_problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
example_problems.why_it_fits: Equivalent to finding the maximum difference between a later and earlier element - can be reframed as a Kadane's-style running max-profit-so-far scan, tracking the minimum price seen so far.

additional_considerations: Always state the initialization of your running variables out loud (negative infinity vs. first element vs. 0) - this is the single most common source of bugs in Kadane's-based solutions, especially with all-negative or single-element edge cases. Mention explicitly whether the problem allows an empty subarray (sum 0) or requires at least one element - this changes the correct initialization.
